solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Awkward task involves delays — time to provide support for Jack? (9)

indicators.note: FAFF takes the other pieces inside it

blocks.note: a faff is a fiddly, time-wasting business

annotation.surface: Someone grumbling about a fiddly, delayed chore they've been handed.
annotation.walkthrough: Jack is the Union Jack, the flag, not a sailor or a car jack. FAFF is informal British for fussing about, here a tiresome task.
annotation.definitionFit: A flagstaff is the pole that holds up a flag such as the Union Jack.

clue.text: Having no set outline available for months (8)

annotation.surface: A planner that has no fixed shape and is open for months ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: The little word 'for' is not a link here; it goes into the answer unchanged.
annotation.definitionFit: Something freeform follows no fixed shape or structure.

clue.text: Conservative and Liberal leaving Essex town for part of London (5)

indicators.note: C and L go out of the town's name

blocks.note: Clacton-on-Sea, a seaside town in Essex

annotation.surface: Two parties' candidates abandoning an Essex seat and moving to London.
annotation.walkthrough: Clacton is a seaside resort in Essex; Acton is a district of west London. The political surface borrows real party abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Acton is one of the districts that make up west London.

clue.text: Increase that’s down to poor middle management? (5,4)

definitions.text: Increase that’s down to poor middle management?

blocks.clueFragment: Increase that’s down to poor middle management?
blocks.note: the surface reading: a rise blamed on weak middle managers in an office
the meant reading: looking after your midriff, so the increase is extra girth

annotation.surface: An office gripe that some rise was caused by weak middle managers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Middle management' reads as an office tier but means looking after your midriff; badly managed, it grows a spare tyre.
annotation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is a roll of fat around the waist, an increase caused by neglecting the middle.

clue.text: Article not equivocal about natural food colouring (7)

indicators.note: an uncertain, ambiguous NOT is rearranged
the rearranged NOT goes round NAT

annotation.surface: A newspaper piece plainly praising a natural food dye.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Natural' looks like part of the definition, but it is only NAT in the wordplay; the definition is just 'food colouring'.
annotation.definitionFit: Annatto is an orange-red dye from achiote seeds, used to colour cheese and other foods.

clue.text: Following deposit, one’s charged — look (7)

blocks.note: ash is the deposit a fire leaves
an ion is a charged particle

annotation.surface: A bank clerk noting that after a deposit, a fee was charged.
annotation.walkthrough: The banking surface hides a chemistry definition of ION and the fireplace sense of deposit.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the style sense: this season's look is its prevailing mode of dress.

clue.text: Catching cold, fancy a hot drink (5)

indicators.note: to catch something is to take hold of it, so COO holds C within it

blocks.note: 'Fancy!' and 'Coo!' are both cries of surprise
C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Someone with a cold who fancies a warming drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' is an exclamation of surprise, like the British 'Coo!', not a wish.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the powder from cacao beans stirred into hot milk is the classic bedtime drink.

clue.text: Fast food joint in Lewis? (5)

indicators.note: a thing 'in' Lewis is placed within his initials, so HIP sits between C and S

blocks.note: C. S. Lewis, author of the Narnia books

annotation.surface: A takeaway on the Isle of Lewis.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fast food joint' reads as one phrase, a takeaway shop; it splits into the definition and HIP. Lewis is the writer, not the Hebridean island.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: fried potato strips are the staple of every takeaway, the fries of American menus.

clue.text: Implement refusal to enter staff room at the outset (3,6)

indicators.note: to enter a place is to go inside it, so NOPE goes into CANE
only the first letter of room is used

blocks.note: a cane is a walking staff

annotation.surface: Management refusing staff entry to their room from the start.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Staff room' is one place in the surface, but staff is a stick and room gives only its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the tool for getting into tins is one of the most ordinary kitchen implements.

clue.text: Upload negatives, inverted and cropped in programme (6)

indicators.note: the letters read upwards, right to left
the outer letters of the phrase are trimmed away

blocks.note: the run of letters inside upLOAD NEGAtives

annotation.surface: Photo-editing instructions: flip and crop the negatives in software.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Programme' is a plan of business, not software; the photo words all do mechanical jobs.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a meeting's list of business to get through is its programme.

clue.text: More quit without one right answer (5)

indicators.note: to be without something is to lack it, so EXIT goes on lacking its I

annotation.surface: Quiz advice: more people give up without getting one answer right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One' is the numeral I, removed from EXIT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in 'extra time' or 'more time' added on.

clue.text: Contemporary, incomplete body of knowledge shows ignorance (9)

indicators.note: NEW loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A complaint that modern, half-baked learning betrays how little we know.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer contains SCIENCE yet means its opposite, from Latin nescire, not to know.
annotation.definitionFit: Nescience is a formal word for lack of knowledge.

clue.text: Two supporters — part of Rovers? (3,4)

annotation.surface: Two fans of a football club called Rovers.
annotation.walkthrough: Rovers looks like a football club, but it means Rover cars; the question mark flags the definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A fan belt is an engine part in a car such as a Rover.

clue.text: Flat’s interior unfinished — overwhelmed, I start to panic (7)

indicators.note: INSIDE loses its last letter
to be overwhelmed is to be engulfed, so I and P are swallowed up inside INSID
only the first letter of panic is used

annotation.surface: Someone inside a half-finished flat, overwhelmed and beginning to panic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flat' reads as an apartment but is the adjective, dull or tasteless; the 's is just 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Insipid means flat, lacking flavour or interest.

clue.text: Refreshing our stock in May and November makes for extensive range (5,9)

indicators.note: the letters are renewed into a new order

annotation.surface: A shopkeeper who restocks twice a year to offer a wide range of goods.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Range' reads as a shop's product line; it is a mountain range.
annotation.definitionFit: The Rocky Mountains are a mountain range stretching thousands of miles through North America.

clue.text: Is able to cross a river in this? (9)

definitions.text: Is able to cross a river in this?

indicators.note: CAN spans A TAMAR, lying across it

blocks.note: the Tamar, dividing Devon from Cornwall

annotation.surface: Asking which boat will get you over a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a catamaran is just the vessel to cross a river in.
annotation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled boat you could cross a river in.

clue.text: Designation of court where, twice, plea is changed, inhibiting start of trial (9)

indicators.note: the letters of PLEA twice are rearranged
the rearranged letters hold T in
only the first letter of trial is used

annotation.surface: A court where a plea is altered twice before the trial even starts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twice' doubles PLEA. The court theme runs through the surface, so the definition hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: An appellate court is one that hears appeals, so 'appellate' designates it.

clue.text: Calmly evacuated ship — danger, primarily, lies within part of engine (8)

indicators.note: CALMLY is emptied, keeping only its outside letters
only the first letter of danger is used
something that lies within another is contained by it, so D rests inside LINER

annotation.surface: A ship calmly abandoned while danger lurks in the engine room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Evacuated' reads as passengers leaving; it means emptying CALMLY of its middle.
annotation.definitionFit: A cylinder is the chamber in an engine where a piston moves.

clue.text: Group ferrying wounded using elastic to protect ear, missing a bit (9,5)

indicators.note: STRETCHY wraps around the inner pieces
a word missing a letter lacks it, so EAR goes without its A

annotation.surface: Medics improvising a bandage with elastic to protect an injured ear.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'a' in 'missing a bit' belongs with 'missing', not with 'bit'.
annotation.definitionFit: A stretcher party is a team carrying the wounded on stretchers.

clue.text: Food supplier from hotel leaving that place in vehicle (7)

indicators.note: H goes out of THERE, as a guest leaving a place departs from it
a passenger in a vehicle is inside it, so TERE rides within CAR

blocks.note: H in the NATO alphabet, removed

annotation.surface: A delivery driver from a hotel heading off to a venue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From' is only a link; the hotel gives the H that THERE loses.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a caterer's whole trade is providing meals for weddings, offices and parties.

clue.text: Barged in front — directed outside behind back of queue (7)

indicators.note: one thing outside another surrounds it, so LED wraps round BOW
what stands behind comes later in line, so the LBOWED unit follows E
only the last letter of queue is used

blocks.note: the bow is the front of a ship

annotation.surface: Someone pushed in at the front of a queue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Barged in front' reads as one queue-jumping phrase; only 'Barged' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To elbow is to push your way through, to barge.

clue.text: Son needs trousers (6)

annotation.surface: A parent's note that a boy needs new trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' reads as a noun the son needs; it is the definition, and 'needs' is the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the loose casual kind of trousers are called slacks.

clue.text: Brilliant line worker receives award (7)

indicators.note: to receive is to take something in, so ANT takes MBE inside itself

blocks.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker
Member of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

annotation.surface: A star factory-line worker gets an honour.
annotation.walkthrough: The MBE is a British honour given to people from all walks of life.
annotation.definitionFit: Lambent means softly glowing or brilliant.

clue.text: Result of being soused regularly? (5)

indicators.note: every other letter is taken

annotation.surface: Asking what happens to someone who gets drunk often.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Soused' is British slang for drunk, and 'regularly' seems to mean often; it picks every second letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense: what results from an action follows on from it as a consequence.

clue.text: Instrument popular with Italy’s premier composer (7)

indicators.note: only the first letter of Italy is used

blocks.note: a bell is a percussion instrument

annotation.surface: An instrument loved by Italy's prime minister and a composer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Premier' looks like a prime minister; it means first letter. Bellini fittingly is Italian.
annotation.definitionFit: Vincenzo Bellini was an Italian opera composer.

clue.text: Frost over vessel circling point south of Island (3,2)

indicators.note: to circle something is to ring it round, so CUP rings E
in a down clue, CEUP comes below I

blocks.note: a cup is a drinking vessel

annotation.surface: Frost forming over a ship sailing round the southern point of an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' belongs with 'Frost' in the definition, not with the wordplay; 'vessel' is a cup, not a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: windscreens and aircraft wings frost over when a layer of ice forms on them.

clue.text: Southern Irish contingent a vital part of wine tasting event (9)

definitions.text: a vital part of wine tasting event

blocks.note: CORK'S: belonging to Cork, a county in the south of Ireland
a crew = a group, a contingent

annotation.surface: A party from southern Ireland being key to a wine tasting.
annotation.walkthrough: Cork is the county and city in the south of Ireland; its crew, CORK'S CREW, is a southern Irish contingent.
annotation.definitionFit: You need a corkscrew to open the bottles at a wine tasting.

clue.text: In two areas, what about Democrat being in front? (5)

indicators.note: HE goes between the two As
'about' as in 'about turn', a turning back, so EH faces the other way

annotation.surface: Asking about a Democrat leading in two districts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'What' is the questioning 'Eh?', not a relative pronoun.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a candidate out in front in the polls is ahead.

clue.text: Pick up clock around noon and head for station (5)

indicators.note: what goes around something surrounds it, so SEE encloses N and S
only the first letter of station is used

blocks.note: to clock something is to see it

annotation.surface: Collecting a clock at midday and making for the railway station.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clock' is British slang for notice, not a timepiece; 'Pick up' is the definition, not a collection.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: you pick up a mood or a signal when you detect it.

clue.text: Food and wine colleague’s keeping very quiet (3,6)

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it, so PEER holds PP inside

blocks.note: a peer is an equal, a colleague
pp = pianissimo, very quiet in music

annotation.surface: A co-worker quietly hoarding the food and wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Food and wine' reads as one pairing; only 'Food' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the ripe sweet capsicum is one food among many.
